Question_text: Kolo owns a successful hairdressing salon in the city centre. He has 4 part-time employees. The business has made a profit in each of the last 3 years. Kolo wants to expand by opening another hairdressing salon to take advantage of the economic boom. He plans to recruit a manager for the second salon using external recruitment. Kolo has identified 2 possible candidates for the position. Information about them is shown in Table 1.1.
image: Table 1.1: Extract from Kolo's information on the two candidates. The table has three rows: Experience, Qualifications, and Other information, and two columns for Candidate 1 and Candidate 2. Candidate 1 has 5 years experience, an Advanced hairdressing certificate, and has never managed a salon. Candidate 2 has 20 years experience, a Basic hairdressing certificate, and uses autocratic leadership style.
Topic: 2.3 Recruitment, selection and training of employees
Sub_topic: Features of leadership: autocratic, democratic, laissez-faire
Stages of business cycle: growth, boom, recession, slump

Parts.part_text: Identify two features of an economic boom.
Identify two stages of the recruitment process.
Outline two possible advantages to Kolo of recruiting a manager.
Explain two reasons why choosing the right location for the new salon is important for Kolo.
Do you think experience is the most important factor for a business to consider when recruiting a new manager? Justify your answer.

Question_text: DSY is a private limited company. It produces washing machines and cleaning equipment. The Managing Director wants DSY to expand into a different market. He plans to spend $2bn on developing electric cars. There is a lot of competition in the electric car market. This market is growing rapidly. A leading pressure group has identified the environmental problems of non-electric cars. The Managing Director knows that important decisions about the method of production and the new car's brand image still have to be made.
Sub_topic: Features: sole traders, partnerships, private/public limited companies, franchises, joint ventures
Brand image: impact on sales, loyalty
Features, benefits, limitations: job, batch, flow production

Parts.part_text: Define 'pressure group'.
Define 'brand image'.
Outline two advantages to DSY of being a private limited company.
Explain two factors DSY should consider when deciding on a suitable method of production for the new product.
Do you think entering a growing market where there is a lot of competition is the best way for a business to expand? Justify your answer.

Question_text: Veronique is bored with her work in a large factory. As a creative person, she would like to leave and start up a flower shop. Veronique has asked about micro-finance and prepared a cash flow forecast. An extract is shown in Table 3.1. Veronique has also carried out some market research and found out that the demand for flowers is likely to be high during festivals. She thinks she has the right characteristics to be a successful entrepreneur.

Sub_topic: What is cash-flow forecast, construction, importance
Overcome short-term problems: overdraft, delay payments, quicker debtor payments

Parts.part_text: Define 'micro-finance'.
Veronique now thinks that the cash inflow in month 3 will be $1500. Calculate the: New net cash flow in month 3:. New closing balance in month 3:
State four reasons why a business might have cash flow problems.

Do you think being creative is the most important characteristic of being a successful entrepreneur? Justify your answer.

Question_text: Gino owns a fast-food restaurant selling fried chicken and potato fries. He employs 5 full-time chefs and 12 part-time workers to serve the food. Communication is important and Gino has regular meetings with his part-time employees to keep them informed about any changes in the menu. It took 3 years before Gino's business was able to break-even. He aims to achieve a Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) of 10%. Gino is always looking for ways to increase the number of customers. Inflation may be a problem for Gino's business.
Topic: 4.2 Costs, scale of production and break-even analysis
Sub_topic: Ratios: gross profit margin, profit margin, return on capital employed, current ratio, acid test ratio
Forms: advertising, sales promotion, influence on sales
Benefits, limitations of methods, including IT

Parts.part_text: Define 'break-even'.
Define 'Return on Capital Employed'.
Outline two problems inflation might cause Gino's business.
Explain two ways Gino could increase the number of customers.
Do you think having regular meetings is a better way for a business to communicate with part-time employees than using text messages? Justify your answer.
